    Plotting a UgridDataset¶

    UgridDataset.plot draws a variable on an unstructured mesh (triangles / polygons) through cleopatra's mesh glyph, sharing the colour vocabulary of the raster path. This gallery plots a static mesh variable, styles it, adds a basemap, then animates a time-varying variable — and finishes on the backend= seam.

    Setup¶

    Inline figures, imports, and the notebook-relative data path (one level deeper than the raster galleries).

    In [1]:
    Copied! 
    %matplotlib inline
from pathlib import Path

from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.dataset import UgridDataset
from pyramids.plot import ColorBar, ColorScaling, Contour, DataStyle

DATA = Path('../../../../examples/data')
    %matplotlib inline from pathlib import Path from pyramids.netcdf.ugrid.dataset import UgridDataset from pyramids.plot import ColorBar, ColorScaling, Contour, DataStyle DATA = Path('../../../../examples/data')

    Load a river-channel mesh with a CRS (EPSG:32631). It carries a static face variable bathymetry and a time-varying face variable water_level.

    In [2]:
    Copied! 
    mesh = UgridDataset.read_file(str(DATA / 'river_channel_ugrid.nc'))
{name: (v.location, v.has_time, v.shape) for name, v in mesh.data_vars.items()}
    mesh = UgridDataset.read_file(str(DATA / 'river_channel_ugrid.nc')) {name: (v.location, v.has_time, v.shape) for name, v in mesh.data_vars.items()}
    Out[2]:
    {'bathymetry': ('face', False, (273,)),
 'water_level': ('face', True, (6, 273)),
 'velocity': ('node', False, (320,))}

    Quickstart¶

    Name the variable; the mesh faces are coloured by its values.

    In [3]:
    Copied! 
    mesh.plot('bathymetry')
    mesh.plot('bathymetry')
    Out[3]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.mesh_glyph.MeshGlyph at 0x7f0389235a90>

    Colormap: cmap=¶

    A mesh takes a Matplotlib colormap name directly through cmap.

    In [4]:
    Copied! 
    mesh.plot('bathymetry', cmap='terrain')
    mesh.plot('bathymetry', cmap='terrain')
    Out[4]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.mesh_glyph.MeshGlyph at 0x7f038893ae90>

    Colour bar and scaling: colorbar= / color=¶

    The same ColorBar and ColorScaling specs as the raster path apply to the mesh glyph.

    In [5]:
    Copied! 
    mesh.plot(
    'bathymetry',
    colorbar=ColorBar(label='bed level [m]'),
    color=ColorScaling.power(gamma=0.7),
)
    mesh.plot( 'bathymetry', colorbar=ColorBar(label='bed level [m]'), color=ColorScaling.power(gamma=0.7), )
    Out[5]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.mesh_glyph.MeshGlyph at 0x7f03887ba990>

    Contours: contour=¶

    A Contour spec draws iso-lines across the mesh.

    In [6]:
    Copied! 
    mesh.plot('bathymetry', contour=Contour(levels=6))
    mesh.plot('bathymetry', contour=Contour(levels=6))
    Out[6]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.mesh_glyph.MeshGlyph at 0x7f03886c4cd0>

    Styling: data_style=¶

    DataStyle applies a cleopatra styling preset to the mesh.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    mesh.plot('bathymetry', data_style=DataStyle(style='flow_accumulation'))
    mesh.plot('bathymetry', data_style=DataStyle(style='flow_accumulation'))
    Out[7]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.mesh_glyph.MeshGlyph at 0x7f0388591950>

    Basemap: basemap=¶

    Because the mesh has a CRS, basemap=True can place a web-tile backdrop beneath it.

    In [8]:
    Copied! 
    mesh.plot('bathymetry', basemap=True)
    mesh.plot('bathymetry', basemap=True)
    Out[8]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.mesh_glyph.MeshGlyph at 0x7f038844d090>

    A time-varying variable¶

    Plotting a temporal variable draws its first time step; the colours now show water level rather than the bed.

    In [9]:
    Copied! 
    mesh.plot('water_level')
    mesh.plot('water_level')
    Out[9]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.mesh_glyph.MeshGlyph at 0x7f038839f390>

    Animation: UgridDataset.animate(...)¶

    animate sweeps the variable over its time axis. For a mesh it returns a matplotlib FuncAnimation directly, which renders to an inline player.

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    from IPython.display import HTML

anim = mesh.animate('water_level', interval=250)
HTML(anim.to_jshtml())
    from IPython.display import HTML anim = mesh.animate('water_level', interval=250) HTML(anim.to_jshtml())
    Out[10]:

    Choosing a renderer with backend=¶

    Every plot and animate method takes a keyword-only backend=. The default, "matplotlib", draws through cleopatra — that is every figure above. Any other name is resolved at call time through the pyramids.plot_backends entry-point group, with an optional fall-back to digitalearth's richer tiers. pyramids declares no dependency on any non-matplotlib renderer, so a bare install always plots through matplotlib.

    backend= Renderer Install
    "matplotlib" (default) cleopatra / matplotlib — static figures included with the [viz] extra
    "interactive" digitalearth (HoloViz / Bokeh) pip install 'digitalearth[interactive]'
    "3d" digitalearth (PyVista) pip install 'digitalearth[3d]'
    "web" digitalearth (MapLibre / deck.gl) pip install 'digitalearth[web]'

    Stating the default explicitly produces exactly the quickstart figure; the digitalearth tiers follow:

    In [11]:
    Copied! 
    mesh.plot('bathymetry', backend='matplotlib')
    mesh.plot('bathymetry', backend='matplotlib')
    Out[11]:
    <cleopatra.glyphs.gridded.mesh_glyph.MeshGlyph at 0x7f0388056d50>

    The digitalearth tiers today¶

    digitalearth's interactive / 3d / web renderers draw raster inputs. A UgridDataset is an unstructured mesh, which digitalearth 0.13 does not yet accept through quickmap, so those backends are not shown here — see the Dataset gallery for live interactive, web and 3-D output on a raster. Wiring UgridDataset support into digitalearth is upstream work in the digitalearth repo; until it lands, UgridDataset.plot renders through matplotlib (every figure above). The backend= seam itself is ready — it already resolves and dispatches to digitalearth the moment digitalearth supports the input type.

    Takeaway¶

    UgridDataset.plot brings the raster colour vocabulary to unstructured meshes — colormap, colour bar, scaling, contours, styling and basemaps — and animate turns a temporal mesh variable into a movie, all routable through backend=.
